source_type: Research report on a national, stratified random survey
reliability: Research institute report of its own national survey; cover dates publication to December 2013, but exact day is unknown. Findings here identify the applicable figure/table and population.
findings: The survey is a national, stratified, random survey of most types of charitable nonprofits reporting $100,000 or more in expenses on IRS Form 990 in 2010.

Urban estimates government agencies entered into about 350,000 contracts and grants with about 56,000 nonprofits; the average is six per nonprofit (median three); governments paid $137 billion to nonprofits for services in 2012.

Figure 11 (printed p. 25), 2013 national survey covering 2012: application complexity 32% big problem + 39% small; reporting complexity 31% big + 40% small; late payments 19% big + 26% small. Missing/not-applicable responses excluded; rounding applies.

The Summary of 2010 Report (printed pp. 6–7) gives about 75% application/reporting and 53% late-payment problem rates for human-service nonprofits in 2009. These must not be attributed to the 2013 survey’s 2012 broader nonprofit population.
Printed p. 32 reports an association between late-payment problems and drawing on reserves, increased credit lines, program reductions and office/site closure; it does not establish causation.

Table 3 (printed p. 10) gives budget-group composition of government-funded nonprofits: 17% in $100k–$249,999, 36% in $250k–$999,999, 31% in $1m–$4.99m, 16% in $5m+. The 17% is not within-band government-funding incidence.
limitations: Data concern 2012; current conditions may differ substantially.
Survey excludes nonprofits under $100,000 in expenses.
Self-reported problems; no dollar cost of administrative effort was extracted.
Publication month December 2013 is stated on the cover; exact day unknown, so published remains null.
Preceding prose around Table 3 is ambiguous; this record uses the explicit column distribution rather than inferring within-band incidence.
The PDF includes an earlier-study summary with a different year and human-service-only population; headline figures must not be mixed across them.
